author: Mark Atwood
text: DESIGN CONSTRAINT 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive, second clarification this session): policy-adapter crates MUST expose batch APIs. This was previously listed as an 'open shape decision' under this epic; that framing was wrong. Per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (just added this session, ratifying 'prevalidation, batch, and caching must remain possible'), batch is a hard requirement for adapter crates with subprocess overhead, not an optimization to be deferred. Reason: subprocess fork+exec is ~10ms; zlint per-cert runtime is microseconds. Per-cert subprocess invocation is a 1000x asymptotic cost penalty, not a constant-factor performance issue. Shape implications for pkix-policy-zlint .1: API includes both a per-cert convenience method AND a batch entry point (something like batch_lint(certs: &[Certificate]) -> Vec<Vec<Finding>>) that spawns zlint once and feeds many certs through stdin or a temp file. Same for pkix-policy-pkilint .2. RESOLVED sub-questions: (c) batch interface shape — must exist; specific bytes-over-stdin vs file-per-cert vs single-call-with-array stays open per implementer. STILL OPEN: lint granularity, severity mapping, error handling, pkix-policy-oscal decision. CACHING NOTE: the Finding type already derives Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq and has serde behind a feature flag (pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:842). Adapter crates inherit that. Caller-side caching of zlint results (key = cert SHA-256 hash; value = Vec<Finding>) is trivially layerable on top. PREVALIDATION NOTE: 'lint these 10,000 certs from a CT log scan, store findings keyed by cert SHA-256, replay on demand' is a supported use case. Adapter crates must not embed non-clonable / non-serializable state in their findings.
